paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God keeps His promises, and He keeps them all the way down the family tree. Matthew 1:1 opens by calling Jesus "the son of David, the son of Abraham." Those are two names God made promises to long before this day, and Matthew starts right there because the promises weren't forgotten. Fourteen generations, then fourteen more, then fourteen more (Matthew 1:17), and the Lord was still on it the whole time.

Now look who made the list: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and "Uriah's wife" (Matthew 1:3, 5, 6). Mess, mistakes and the exile to Babylon are all in that family line, and Jesus still came right through it. So if your own story has some chapters you'd rather skip, hear me, friend. God doesn't need a spotless record to do something wonderful. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and He still had work for me!

Then comes Joseph, stuck in the middle of a heartbreaking moment, and the angel tells him the Son's name: Jesus, "because He will save His people from their sins" (Matthew 1:21). That's the whole reason He came. The prophet's name for Him, Immanuel, means "God with us" (Matthew 1:23), and that's the promise worth carrying out of this passage. When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel commanded (Matthew 1:24), and that's our move too: trust Him, then do what He says. And friend, this story is only getting started.
